hints: Focus on how hot, concentrated KMnO4 completely breaks the C=C double bond, with each alkene carbon becoming a separate carbonyl product.
Remember the cleavage rule: a carbon with two alkyl groups, R2C=, becomes a ketone, while a carbon with one H, RCH=, becomes a carboxylic acid.
Check each of the three alkenes for one disubstituted end and one monosubstituted end to see if you get one of each product type.
walkthrough:
**Recall oxidative cleavage rule**

Hot, concentrated, acidified KMnO4 cleaves the alkene at the double bond. Each C of the C=C is oxidised separately.

$$\text{R}_2\text{C=CR}_2 \rightarrow \text{ketone + ketone}$$
$$\text{R}_2\text{C=CHR} \rightarrow \text{ketone + RCOOH}$$
$$\text{RCH=CHR} \rightarrow \text{2 carboxylic acids}$$

**Analyse compound 1**

Compound 1 is $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C=CHCH}(\text{CH}_3)_2$. The left carbon has two methyl groups, the right carbon has one H and one alkyl group.

$$ (\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C=} \rightarrow (\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C=O, a ketone} $$
$$ \text{=CHCH}(\text{CH}_3)_2 \rightarrow (\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHCOOH, a carboxylic acid} $$
So 1 gives a ketone plus a carboxylic acid.

**Analyse compounds 2 and 3**

Compound 2 is $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{CCH=C}(\text{CH}_2)_4$. The left carbon is RCH=, the right carbon is part of a ring with two alkyl bonds.

$$\text{left} \rightarrow (\text{CH}_3)_3\text{CCOOH, a carboxylic acid}$$
$$\text{right} \rightarrow \text{cyclopentanone, a ketone}$$
Compound 3 is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH=C}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)_2$. The left carbon is RCH=, the right carbon has two alkyl groups.

$$\text{left} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{COOH, a carboxylic acid}$$
$$\text{right} \rightarrow \text{ketone}$$
So 2 and 3 also give one ketone plus one carboxylic acid. Therefore 1, 2 and 3 are all correct.

options.A: Correct. All three alkenes are of the type R2C=CHR. Cleavage gives R2C=O (ketone) from the disubstituted end and RCOOH (carboxylic acid) from the monosubstituted end in every case.
options.B: Incorrect. This omits compound 3. Compound 3 is CH3CH=C(CH3)CH(CH3)2, so it also has one R2C= end for a ketone and one RCH= end for ethanoic acid.
options.C: Incorrect. This omits compound 1. Compound 1 is (CH3)2C=CHCH(CH3)2, so it clearly gives propanone (ketone) plus 2-methylpropanoic acid.
options.D: Incorrect. This includes only compound 1. Both compounds 2 and 3 also fit the pattern, with 2 giving cyclopentanone plus an acid, and 3 giving a ketone plus ethanoic acid.
